title: Life-cycle assessment
examples: How do you compare the environmental impact of different materials?
What are the main stages in a life-cycle assessment?
Can you give an example of a product we can assess this way?

explain.say: Today we will learn about life-cycle assessment.
The first stage looks at getting raw materials from the earth.
Next, we look at making the product in a factory setting.
The use phase covers how we actually use the product over time.
Finally, we consider what happens when the product is thrown away.
For example, when comparing paper and plastic bags, we must look at all these steps.

faq.q: What is the main purpose of a life-cycle assessment?
faq.a: It helps us see the total environmental impact of a product. It looks at everything from start to finish.
asks: Why do we need to assess a product's life cycle?
What does 'life-cycle' mean in this context?

faq.q: Does the use phase always count the most impact?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Sometimes the raw material stage or disposal can be the biggest problem.
asks: Is the use phase always the biggest part?

faq.q: What does 'biodegradable' mean in this assessment?
faq.a: It means natural materials can break down safely over time. This is important for the end-of-life stage.
asks: What is the difference between biodegradable and compostable?

faq.q: Do we have to assess every single product?
faq.a: No, we usually focus on products where the environmental impact is a major concern. This helps guide better choices.
asks: Do we need to do this for every item?

faq.q: What is the difference between recycling and composting?
faq.a: Recycling turns materials into new items. Composting breaks down organic matter into soil nutrients.
asks: Which is better for the environment?

facts: A life-cycle assessment looks at a product from 'cradle to grave'.
Key stages include raw material extraction, manufacturing, use, and disposal.
Impacts assessed can include energy use, water pollution, and greenhouse gases.
Biodegradable items break down naturally over time.

quiz.say: When assessing a product, which stage considers the energy used while the product is being used?
quiz.why: The use phase directly measures the energy or resources consumed while the product is actively in use.

wrong.0: This stage focuses only on the factory processes to build the item.
wrong.1: This stage only deals with what happens after the product is thrown away.
wrong.3: This stage only covers getting the basic ingredients from the earth.

quiz.say: If a product is made from wood, which stage involves cutting the trees?
quiz.why: Cutting down trees is the very first step, which is raw material extraction.

wrong.1: Manufacturing happens after the raw material has already been collected.
wrong.2: The use phase happens when you are actually using the finished product.
wrong.3: Disposal is the final step, after the product has been used up.

quiz.say: Which process turns organic waste into soil nutrients?
quiz.why: Composting is the specific process that breaks down organic matter into useful soil components.

wrong.0: Landfilling is just putting waste in a pile, not actively breaking it down.
wrong.1: Incineration burns waste, which releases gases, unlike composting.
wrong.3: Recycling usually means turning materials into new manufactured items, not soil.
